dish: Erie Greek dog — a skinless Smith's wiener on a warm bun under mustard, onions and slow-cooked Greek meat sauce
w: Opened 1927 and claims to be the first place to serve Erie's signature Greek dog; the Greek sauce is a spiced-up Greek pasta-sauce recipe brought by the city's early Greek restaurateurs, and it's the defining Erie street food.

dish: Char-grilled Smith's hot dogs and homemade orange-vanilla twist soft-serve
w: The seasonal 1950s-themed drive-in guarding the entrance to Presque Isle since 1980 — vintage gas pumps, red picnic tables, char-grilled Smith's dogs and orange-vanilla twist; lines can run an hour at peak.

dish: Pepperoni ball — pepperoni and mozzarella rolled in handmade dough and deep-fried, Erie-style (not the WV baked pepperoni roll)
w: Making Erie's deep-fried pepperoni balls since 1961; so central to the city's identity that the Erie SeaWolves rebranded as the 'Pepperoni Balls' and QVC sold out 18,000 of Stanganelli's frozen ones in 2020.

dish: Sponge candy — crunchy honeycomb toffee sponge dipped in chocolate, the signature confection of the Lake Erie 'Sponge Candy Crescent'
w: A four-generation Erie chocolatier whose sponge candy (and sponge-candy truffles) is a benchmark for the regional treat that can only be made in cool, dry weather; Erie sits in the heart of the 'Sponge Candy Crescent.'

dish: Sponge candy and hand-dipped chocolates, with a walk-through candy-factory tour
w: Erie chocolatier tracing to Greek immigrant George Pulakos in 1889; known for sponge taffy, French truffles and a 25-minute factory tour with samples — the old-guard counterpart to Romolo in Erie's chocolate scene.

dish: House craft ales in one of downtown Erie's busiest taprooms, with a full food menu
w: A cornerstone of the Lake Erie Ale Trail — a downtown Erie brewery whose taproom is among the city's busiest, pouring a wide range of styles alongside a well-reviewed kitchen.

dish: Handcrafted ales served inside a 1927 railroad station that's still an active Amtrak stop
w: A brewpub set in Erie's historic Union Station — trains still stop upstairs — pairing fresh house ales with a scratch menu; consistently rated among the best restaurants in the city.

dish: Year-round and seasonal ales from a Great American Beer Festival medalist
w: Founded as a brewpub in 1993 and a full brewery since 1999, Erie Brewing has taken three Great American Beer Festival medals and distributes across more than a dozen states — the veteran of the local scene.

dish: Chef's-table modern Asian and sushi tasting menus
w: Chef Dan Kern's small downtown room built around an open chef's counter and inventive Asian-leaning tasting plates; a repeat Erie Reader 'Best of Erie' honoree (Best Chef runner-up, 2018).

dish: Family-recipe traditional Italian pastas and red-sauce classics
w: Family-owned since 1999, cooking authentic Italian from recipes passed down for generations — a locals' pick for Erie's Italian dining rooted in the city's deep Italian community.

dish: Texas-style smoked brisket and BBQ on the edge of Erie's Little Italy
address: W 26th St & Peach St, Erie, PA 16508
w: Bringing slow-smoked Texas barbecue to far-northern PA near Erie's Little Italy at 26th and Peach; a frequently top-cited Erie meat destination.

dish: Estate wines in Lake Erie Wine Country, from Concord-belt varieties to European vinifera
address: 11815 East Lake Rd, North East, PA 16428
w: Built in 1972 by brothers Robert and Frank Mazza in Mediterranean style, the flagship of Lake Erie Wine Country and the family's North East operations (which include the historic South Shore Wine Company) — the anchor of the PA grape belt's wine scene.

dish: Lake Erie AVA wines from one of Pennsylvania's oldest modern wineries
address: 10225 East Lake Rd, North East, PA 16428
w: One of the first two wineries in Pennsylvania to get a limited-winery license after Prohibition (1968), crushing its first grapes in 1969 — a foundational stop on the Lake Erie Wine Country trail.

dish: Estate wines and fruit wines from a 250-acre North East farm
address: 12073 East Main Rd, North East, PA 16428
w: Nick and Kathy Mobilia's farm winery since 1998, making wine from grapes and fruit grown on their own 250 acres — European varietals (Pinot Grigio, Riesling) alongside native Niagara, Catawba and Concord.

dish: House craft beer and pub fare at the birthplace of Voodoo Brewing
w: The original home of Voodoo Brewing Co., founded in Meadville in 2005 with its first taproom opening here in 2012 before the brand grew into 20-plus locations nationwide — the corridor's most consequential craft-beer origin story.

dish: Farm-to-table comfort food and signature craft ales in a downtown Slippery Rock brewpub
address: 141 S Main St, Slippery Rock, PA 16057
w: An early western-PA craft adopter (2005), North Country's Slippery Rock brewpub ranks #1 in town, pairing house beers with farm-to-table fare from wings and burgers to salmon and crab cakes; it also runs the historic Harmony Inn.

dish: German-leaning tavern fare in a reputedly haunted 1856 building
w: A historic tavern in the heart of Harmony's National Historic Landmark district, now run by North Country Brewing, serving German-inflected comfort food in a storied (and reputedly haunted) old building.

dish: Estate wines and small-batch spirits on Pennsylvania's largest natural lake
w: A lakeside winery and distillery beside Conneaut Lake that hosts summer live-music and outdoor tasting series — the drinks anchor of the Conneaut Lake resort area on the corridor.
